text:
maya: heads up — provisioning backlog for GPU jobs in az1. pods stuck at ContainerCreating on nodes i-az1-10/11. noticed huge iowait on local NVMe. anyone looking?
chris: yep seeing the same. iowait ~98% on /dev/nvme1n1, ephemeral-cleaner logs show repeated lock timeouts. kube-scheduler backlog ~120 pods waiting for GPU nodes.
infra-bot: ALERT: metric nvme_iowait > 85% (ephemeral-pool-az1) — triggered at 2026-03-16T10:07:12Z
sam: can we evict the cleaner or drain one node and reboot? need short term to unblock provisioning.
lee: cleaner got a change yesterday to do parallel deletes, might be hammering iops. fallback path didn't land. thinking the parallel jobs are causing hotspots on NVMe.
chris: digging into logs — paste: ```
Mar 16 10:05:43 i-az1-10 systemd[1]: Started ephemeral-cleaner.
ephemeral-cleaner[2345]: deleting /var/scratch/job-*/cache
ephemeral-cleaner[2345]: error: lock timeout acquiring /var/lock/ephemeral-cleaner
``` 
maya: oof. that lock timeout loop would keep retries and chew iops. we should throttle cleaner to 1 worker asap.
sam: agree. i'll open a quick k8s rollout to set `CLEANER_WORKERS=1` for az1 daemonset and patch live.
chris: temporary mitigation — cordon i-az1-11 and drain non-gpu pods; freeing some IO for the cleaner to finish. starting now.
lee: FYI the scheduler binds GPU pods to these nodes because warm pool has local-ssd affinity. if we can't free nodes we should scale warm pool with spare instances (no nvme-heavy init).
maya: starting warm-pool scale +2 in az1 (using instance type with EBS-only). that should buy us time.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260316-az1-nvme-wedge by maya — https://incident/INC-20260316-az1-nvme-wedge
chris: cleaner rollout applied to az1 with 1 worker, replicas updated.
sam: evictions done, pods transitioned to Running for ~30 pods so far. iowait dropping to ~45%.
lee: still seeing a couple of corrupted temp files in logs but nothing filesystem-level. might be partial deletes during retries.
maya: plan: revert parallel-cleaner change in next deploy, add a bounded-rate limiter for deletes, and add a pre-flight check to avoid running on nodes with >70% iowait. create a follow-up ticket.
chris: will follow up on pod scheduling metrics to ensure we don't keep pinning to hot NVMe nodes.
maya: thanks all. keeping channel updated, will post incident postmortem when we stabilize. :thumbsup:
